purpose: Router-visible degraded-evidence replay pack focused on misleading incidents, conflicting telemetry, partial fixes, and delayed root causes.

cases.title: Auto-fix appeared to work but final state drifted after re-fetch
cases.symptom: A reconciliation flow reported progress after an auto-fix step, but later state checks still diverged.
visible_evidence: The same workflow both mutates state and re-fetches it later
A first apparent correction may not reflect the final settled state
This looks like degraded evidence rather than a simple one-pass handler bug

starting_context.repro_style: re-fetch ambiguity / partial fix history / conflicting telemetry

success_criteria: identify why apparent fix progress did not guarantee final convergence
propose a fix family consistent with the landed re-fetch and auto-fix changes
cases.notes: Designed to test whether the router resists premature convergence after a first visible success.

cases.title: Report flow failed across nested response and partner-resolution paths
cases.symptom: A report flow failed because upstream response shape and partner resolution did not line up consistently.
visible_evidence: The bug crosses request construction, fallback resolution, and upstream response parsing
Multiple plausible local fixes exist, but the issue spans more than one boundary
This is a cross-system ambiguity case, not just a flat mapping typo

misleading_telemetry: first failure can appear to be missing input only
response shape looks valid in some paths but not others

success_criteria: identify the cross-boundary failure between partner resolution and response handling
propose a fix family consistent with the landed multi-surface patch
cases.notes: Good degraded-evidence case because input resolution and response interpretation can each look like the sole problem.

cases.title: Approval flow returned an ambiguous 200
cases.symptom: An approval flow returned HTTP 200, but the result could not safely be treated as a successful approval.
visible_evidence: The surface status code suggests success while the contract signal remains ambiguous
The safe fix is about interpretation and fail-closed behavior, not just transport success
This is a conflicting-telemetry case where naive narrowing can trust the wrong signal

entry_points: base URL selection for remote approval call

misleading_telemetry: payload may omit an explicit success signal

success_criteria: identify why a nominally successful response still required fail-closed handling
propose a fix family consistent with the landed contract interpretation change

cases.title: Public audit facade looked plausible while contract and env state were unsafe
cases.symptom: A public audit path could return plausible-looking output even when backend row shape or environment inputs were unsafe.
visible_evidence: The issue is not a single exception path; it is a contract trust problem plus environment validation
User-facing output can look acceptable while the underlying mapping is invalid
This is a deceptive facade case rather than a narrow serialization typo

starting_context.repro_style: public-facade contract mismatch / env validation ambiguity

misleading_telemetry: request shape may appear valid before stricter checks

success_criteria: identify why the facade needed fail-closed mapping and stricter env validation
propose a fix family consistent with the landed public-facade hardening

cases.title: Rollover allowances stopped working after refresh and publisher updates
cases.symptom: Allowance rollover behavior failed after later refresh or publisher-update activity even though earlier flows looked correct.
visible_evidence: The bug spans task flow, helper logic, and publisher update behavior
It has the shape of a partial-fix or stale-state problem rather than a single local decrement issue
The correct move may require following the post-refresh state path, not just the immediate limit math
success_criteria: identify why the rollover logic broke after later state changes
propose a fix family consistent with the landed multi-surface patch
cases.notes: Good degraded-evidence backend case with delayed failure after seemingly correct earlier state.
